claims.quote: A multi-ciliated epithelial cell located in the trachea and bronchi, characterized by a columnar shape and motile cilia on its apical surface.

claims.quote: Cilia are found on many cells of the body, including the epithelial cells that line the airways of the respiratory system. Cilia move rhythmically; they beat constantly, moving waste materials such as dust, mucus, and bacteria upward through the airways, away from the lungs and toward the mouth.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Its cilia move mucus and the particles trapped in it toward the pharynx, clearing the airway (mucociliary clearance).
claims.quote: These cilia facilitate mucociliary clearance by moving mucus and trapped particles toward the pharynx.

source.section: CL:0002145 multiciliated columnar cell of tracheobronchial tree

claims.value: With the rest of the ciliated airway lining it forms a mucociliary escalator, sweeping dust and pathogens trapped in mucus toward the throat.
claims.quote: The ciliated epithelium of your airway forms a mucociliary escalator that sweeps particles of dust and pathogens trapped in the secreted mucus toward the throat.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

tier1.text: A multi-ciliated epithelial cell located in the trachea and bronchi, characterized by a columnar shape and motile cilia on its apical surface. These cilia facilitate mucociliary clearance by moving mucus and trapped particles toward the pharynx.
